## Summary

Eisman reduces exposure after a rapid technology-led rally, emphasizing speculative positioning, war risk and producer inflation while maintaining his no-recession view. He separates healthier banks from a risky private-credit cycle, prefers network moats in payments, and continues to favor AI infrastructure and Meritage while short FICO. Cisco results support the supplier thesis. His near-term Coinbase profit prediction is ambiguous because GAAP losses persisted while adjusted EBITDA was positive.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

## Framework and tools

- Distinguish risk reduction from predicting recession.
- Watch funding conditions at lenders as well as borrower defaults.
- Separate strong reported growth from demanding expectations.
- Disclose positions and specify the actual business thesis.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Sector index weights and retail option positioning.
- Producer inflation and Treasury yields.
- FSK sponsor capital and credit facilities.
- Cisco AI orders and Meritage tangible book.
